decisions_for_user: ON THE REVIEW PAGE as DAY-1 (new, iteration 6): the merge gate's two hardest conditions chase each other and it needs rewording. CI is 10-16 minutes on this branch, so a firing that commits before checking fails the CI condition and one that checks late fails the tree-clean condition. It opened at iteration 3 only because a manoeuvre was improvised on the spot (R1's untracked output moved to %TEMP%). The page proposes letting the gate fast-forward to the newest CI-GREEN commit on the branch rather than requiring that commit to be HEAD, and states that iteration 2 considered exactly this and refused it correctly -- the limits authorise a fast-forward to the branch, not to a sha chosen inside it. Answer in DIRECTION.md.

ON THE REVIEW PAGE as DAY-2 (carried, narrowed a third time): F295 is filed severity A on a production claim no round could establish by measurement, and all three rounds narrowed it rather than widening it. R1 found no in-process loop close outside process exit; R2 re-derived that negative independently and it held, and established the worker threads are daemon because SQLAlchemy makes them so; R3 measured that `agentweave stop` on Windows force-kills and runs no shutdown at all, and measured one of R2's two test-suite paths FALSE (dispose calls pool.recreate(), so it is a file-handle leak -- F292's subject -- not a reuse path). The test-suite half is now ONE unrun path. So: does F295 keep its A, and is the change worth a night slot on shutdown-hygiene and test-harness value alone? R3 gave a second reason: the fix as originally specced would itself have hung the shutdown.

ON THE REVIEW PAGE as DAY-3 (new, iteration 5, now on the page): F297 (B) -- `agentweave stop` on Windows runs `taskkill /PID <pid> /F` with no signal first, so the Hub's lifespan shutdown never runs and `terminate_all_active_runs()` is skipped, against the shipped app-lifecycle scenario. Measured, not reasoned. Deliberately kept OUT of the F295 change. Does it get its own spec loop, and before or after F295's implementation? They interact -- a graceful Windows stop would start running the shutdown sequence F295's change is adding -- so landing F295 first is the safer order.
